The Svitolina chain (Eala handled her; she handled Anisimova) is the cleanest same-surface, same-fortnight comparison and it points at Eala. First career meeting, so no H2H baggage; Eala rested Aug 10-15 and her opener was short. I make it a true coin flip, ~50% for Eala against a 46-cent ask — a thin but real value edge on the in-form side.

key_factors.note: 8-1 hard swing with wins over Pegula, Osaka, Svitolina, Zheng; Anisimova's best recent win is #50 Sonmez
Anisimova's left wrist caused a retirement and 3 straight withdrawals in 2026; form never recovered
Eala d. Svitolina 6-3 6-4 (DC); Svitolina d. Anisimova 6-2 6-4 (Toronto) days apart
Flat first-strike power is Eala's kryptonite — Bencic won 6-4 6-0 with that template a week ago
American at home, night session on P&G Center Court; Eala deep into a 10-match, 3-week stretch

rows.tail_risk: Anisimova's peak is far above Eala's: a 2025 dual Slam finalist and two-time WTA 1000 champ whose flat hitting mirrors Bencic, who just blew Eala out 6-4 6-0. If the wrist is clean and she strikes early at home, Eala gets rushed and this loses in under 80 minutes.

rows.title: Noskova vs Tauson
rows.tournament: Cincinnati Open WTA 1000, Round of 32 (R3), outdoor hard
rows.headline: Rested Wimbledon champ vs fatigued, injury-riddled Tauson on next-day turnaround
rows.analysis: Noskova (WTA No. 7, reigning Wimbledon champion — beat Keys, Mertens, Kostyuk and Muchova in that run) meets Tauson (No. 30, 14-18 in 2026) with every current factor leaning her way. Noskova answered her Toronto letdown loss to McNally (No. 64) with a clean 6-3 6-3 over Boulter on Aug 15 and gets a full rest day. Tauson needed 2h45m in 30C+ heat to escape Peyton Stearns (No. 54) 7-6(7) 1-6 7-5 on Aug 16 and must return ~24h later for a 13:20 start in August heat — historically her weak spot (documented heat struggles in Cincinnati 2025, wheelchair-assisted retirement in Guangzhou), on top of a 2026 littered with retirements/withdrawals (Adelaide, Madrid shoulder, Rome back/shoulder). Tauson's 2-0 H2H (AO 2025, Dubai 2025) is stale — it came at her peak (No. 12) and before Noskova's breakout. Books devig to ~67-68% Noskova and models say 68-69%, but the turnaround/fitness asymmetry looks underpriced; I make it ~72%, so 0.69 offers a modest edge with the fundamentals stacked one way.

key_factors.note: Tauson played 2h45m in heat Aug 16, back on court ~24h later; Noskova rested since Aug 15
Wimbledon champion, No. 7 vs No. 30 with a 14-18 season; best recent Tauson win is Stearns (No. 54)
Tauson's 2026: Adelaide ret., Madrid W/D (shoulder), Rome ret. (back/shoulder); known heat struggles
2-0 Tauson on hard (7-6(4) 6-4 Dubai; 5-7 6-3 6-4 AO 2025), but 18 months stale

rows.tail_risk: Tauson's first-strike serve+forehand game has beaten Noskova twice on hard and can win without long rallies even when tired; Noskova's post-Slam wobble (McNally loss, 68 unforced-error tendencies in tight sets) means a flat day loses to a hot server at any fitness level.

rows.title: Parry vs Boisson
rows.tournament: Cincinnati Open (WTA 1000) third round, outdoor hard
rows.headline: Parry's wins are real (Mertens 3 sets); Boisson's form is 1 match + a retirement, on a rebuilt knee
rows.analysis: All-French 3R in Cincinnati, no prior H2H. Parry (#64, only French woman in top 100) has the far sturdier case: she beat Dolehide 6-4 7-6(7) and #22 seed Mertens 2-6 6-2 6-2 in 2h20 — full-distance hard-court wins over quality opposition. Boisson (#281-299, wildcard) is the bigger talent (RG 2025 semifinalist, CH #34) but her ranking collapse is injury-driven: out Sept 2025-April 2026, a knee injury at Wimbledon in July, and by her own words '18 months of rehab out of the last 26.' Her Cincinnati form is one real win (Krueger 6-3 6-2, a boom-or-bust opponent) plus 43 minutes before Bencic retired — softer than it looks. Books make Boisson -120/Parry +104 (Dimers 51.8/48.2), pricing her ceiling but arguably underpricing fragility: this is her third match in five days on back-to-back days, her densest load since the comeback, in Cincinnati heat, against a slicer whose low, pace-less balls force her to generate from the knees. Boisson is fresher (44 min vs 2h20 yesterday), which is her best card, but Parry is 23, fit, and match-tough. The mid-match retirement tail sits entirely on Boisson's side, and every ride goes to settlement. Parry at 0.49 vs fair ~0.53 is the value side of the coin flip.

Boisson: 7-month layoff to April 2026, knee injury at Wimbledon in July; retirement tail risk is hers

rows.tail_risk: Boisson's healthy level is genuinely higher — she beat Pegula and Andreeva at RG 2025 — and sharps made her the favorite. If her knee holds and the forehand lands like it did vs Krueger, she can overpower Parry, whose hard-court record outside this week (Day, Hontama losses) is shaky.

rows.title: Valentova vs Svitolina
rows.tournament: Cincinnati Open (WTA 1000) R64/2nd round, outdoor hard, Lindner Family Tennis Center, Mason OH, P&G Stadium Court
rows.headline: Valentova a set up 6-3 on a leggy Svitolina, yet still priced as the underdog
rows.analysis: This match is live and the market quote looks behind the play. ESPN's scoreboard and TennisMajors independently show Valentova took the first set 6-3, with the second set at 0-0 and Valentova serving; no site anywhere has published a final, and tennisexplorer's Aug 16 results page does not list it as completed. Pre-match, Svitolina (WTA No. 9, 8th seed) was roughly a 70-73% favorite over Valentova (No. 64, live ~56), and every preview tipped a Svitolina straight-setter. A set down flips that: a ~30% underdog who wins set one is normally 60-65% to close, and the set win is itself evidence Valentova is playing above her number today. The setup supports it. Svitolina, 31, is on her first match in Cincinnati straight off five matches in Toronto and a 10-match win streak, including three-set grinds with Alexandrova and Swiatek (6-3 1-6 6-3, Aug 12). That is a textbook post-deep-run letdown spot against a 19-year-old who already has a completed match in these hot, humid conditions. They have never met, so there is no scar tissue for the teenager. At 0.45 ask I am buying a leading player.

key_factors.note: Won set 1 6-3 per ESPN and TennisMajors; set 2 at 0-0 on her serve. Market still has her at 0.44.
Svitolina: 5 Toronto matches, 10-match streak, 3-set SF loss Aug 12, then travel. First match here.
Valentova already banked a Cincinnati R1 win (6-2 7-6(4) over Stoiana); Svitolina is cold.
No. 9, 41-12 in 2026 with two titles, elite fitness and one of the tour's best three-set fighters.
Valentova is 19 and wobbled from 4-1 up in set 2 of R1 vs a qualifier before needing a tiebreak.
First ever meeting; no prior book on either side.
Outdoor hard suits both; Valentova 13-9 on hard in 2026, Svitolina a career hard-court stalwart.
